title: Salvation and Good Works
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Salvation and good works teaches that good works do not earn salvation, but they necessarily flow from saving grace. Believers are saved by grace through faith and created in Christ Jesus for good works.
summary: Salvation and good works teaches that good works do not earn salvation, but they necessarily flow from saving grace. Believers are saved by grace through faith and created in Christ Jesus for good works.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves His people apart from their works, yet He also makes them a people who bear fruit for God. Good works display the life and grace He has given.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture clearly denies that sinners are saved by works. Salvation is a gift of grace through faith, not a reward for human achievement.

Yet Scripture also teaches that saving faith is not barren. God saves His people for good works prepared beforehand. Works are not the root of salvation, but they are fruit of salvation.

James warns against a dead faith that claims belief but has no evidence of life. This does not contradict justification by faith; it shows that genuine faith is living and fruitful.

Good works must remain connected to Christ. Apart from Him, people can do outwardly impressive things but cannot bear fruit that glorifies God as the work of saving grace.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people use works to try to earn acceptance with God. Others use grace as an excuse for fruitlessness. This doctrine corrects both legalism and lawlessness.

It also gives clarity in discipleship. Growth, service, mercy, obedience, and love matter deeply, but they must be taught as fruit of grace, not payment for salvation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do good works from grace, not for grace. Reject both prideful performance and passive disobedience. Ask whether your life shows the fruit of faith, and serve others as one who has already been loved and saved by Christ.
